recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — say what |x − 2| becomes for x < 2 and why that sign is the one to use.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write |x − 2| for x < 2
steps.margin_note: First mark. The sign is the whole question. x → 2⁻ means x approaches 2 through values LESS than 2, so x − 2 is negative and the modulus changes the sign.
steps.memory_tip: |t| = t when t is positive and −t when t is negative. Left of 2 means x − 2 is negative, so the minus is the one that applies.
lines: By definition, |t| = t when t ≥ 0 and |t| = −t when t < 0.
x → 2⁻ means x approaches 2 through values with x < 2.
For x < 2 we have x − 2 < 0, so |x − 2| = −(x − 2)

recall.must_convey: That x → 2⁻ means x < 2, so x − 2 is negative and |x − 2| = −(x − 2).
accept: x tends to two from the left so x is less than two
x minus two is negative so the modulus is minus of x minus two
mod of a negative number is the negative of it
x rendu kanna thakkuva kabatti x minus two negative avuthundi
left hand limit means x is below two

steps.why: The modulus cannot be removed until the sign of x − 2 is known, and only the side of the approach settles it. This is the one-sided part of the question, so stating x < 2 in words is what earns the mark.
common_mistakes: Writing |x − 2| = x − 2, which is the rule for the right-hand side.
Substituting x = 2 and writing 0/0; x never takes the value 2 in a one-sided limit.

steps.label: Cancel (x − 2)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The expression is equal to −1 at every x < 2, not only in the limit, so the limit is −1. On the right of 2 the same working gives +1.
steps.memory_tip: Left of the point gives −1, right of the point gives +1. The two sides disagree, which is why the limit at 2 itself does not exist.
lines: For x < 2 we also have x ≠ 2, so (x − 2) ≠ 0 and may be cancelled:
This holds for every x < 2, so the value stays −1 as x approaches 2 from the left.

recall.must_convey: That −(x − 2)/(x − 2) cancels to −1 for every x < 2, so the left-hand limit is −1.
accept: minus x minus two over x minus two cancels to minus one
the value is minus one for every x below two
so the left hand limit is minus one
it is a constant minus one on the left side

steps.why: The value −1 is given, so the marks are for the reasoning that reaches it. After the modulus is removed the expression is the constant −1 on the whole left side, and a constant function has that constant as its limit.
common_mistakes: Cancelling to +1 by dropping the minus sign taken out of the modulus.
Saying the limit does not exist — that is true at x = 2 two-sided, but the question asks only for the left-hand limit.

insider_note: The left-hand arrow is the whole question: x < 2 makes x − 2 negative, so |x − 2| = −(x − 2). The ratio is then the constant −1 for every x below 2.
